characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy lever controls the project's ability to demonstrate a secure, platform-neutral authentication method. Its objectives are to showcase technical feasibility and credibility in procurement negotiations. Key success metrics include the development of demonstrators that can be used as evidence for policy traction.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) because a credible technical demonstration will strengthen the coalition's argument for platform-neutral access. It also has synergy with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3), as a secure, open standards-based authentication method can be promoted to European bodies.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) because focusing on a single, highly secure authentication method may limit the project's ability to influence procurement decisions that require flexibility and multiple options. A conflict also arises with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633), as prioritizing technical feasibility over policy considerations may lead to a disconnect between the project's goals and its advocacy efforts.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy lever controls the project's ability to shape procurement decisions through effective policy advocacy. Its objectives are to influence AltID requirements and increase adoption of platform-neutral standards. Key success metrics include the submission of policy proposals and the likelihood of influencing AltID requirements.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) because a broad coalition can amplify the project's advocacy efforts. It also has synergy with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474), as credible technical demonstrations can strengthen policy arguments.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever conflicts with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) because prioritizing policy advocacy over procurement influence may lead to a disconnect between the project's goals and its ability to shape procurement decisions. A conflict also arises with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3), as focusing on domestic policy may limit the project's ability to influence European standards.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy controls the breadth and depth of support for platform-neutral digital identity. By building a coalition that includes security experts, contingency-planning stakeholders, civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers, this strategy amplifies advocacy efforts. The immediate consequence is increased stakeholder engagement, leading to a 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions. This strategic lever has the potential to create greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633) as they both contribute to a unified message and increased influence. The technical feasibility of platform-neutral digital identity, provided by the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474), also supports this lever's goals.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever may conflict with the options for the Coalition Building Strategy that focus on building a narrow coalition, as they might limit the breadth of support. Additionally, actively recruiting dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen could potentially create internal debate, hindering the coalition's effectiveness.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy controls the adoption of platform-neutral digital identity through procurement influence. By including specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths in AltID procurement documents, this strategy drives adoption. The immediate consequence is the inclusion of platform-neutral language in procurement documents, leading to 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity. This strategic lever has the potential to reduce long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) as it relies on credible technical demonstrations to support its goals. The EU Standards Engagement Strategy (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3) also supports this lever's goals by promoting standards that reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever may conflict with the options for the Procurement Influence Strategy that focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk, as they might be less effective in driving adoption. Additionally, proposing a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring could potentially create opportunities for vendors to game the system.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy aims to influence relevant European Union bodies and technical working groups to adopt platform-neutral access requirements and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards. This lever seeks to enhance interoperability, reduce lock-in across Europe, and increase alignment with the European Digital Identity Wallet framework.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551), as both aim to promote platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms. The Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474) also benefits from this lever, as successful EU standards engagement can provide a solid foundation for the development of non-production demonstrators.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever may conflict with the Policy Advocacy Strategy (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633), as the EU standards engagement might not align perfectly with domestic policy goals. Additionally, there is a risk that large platform vendors could influence EU standards to favor their interests, undermining the effectiveness of this lever.
